title: Natalia Milosz-Piekarska: Sifted Light at MPRG
summary: Sculptural and wearable jewellery works translating the beauty of the Mornington Peninsula into poetic form. Guided by deep connection to land and sea. Free entry.
recurrenceNote: Open Sat–Sun 11am–4pm (check MPRG for weekday hours)
suitableFor: Adults, families, art lovers, Peninsula locals with an interest in jewellery and craft
nearbyAttractions: Mornington foreshore; Main Street cafes; Mornington Pier
suggestedItineraryPairing: See both MPRG exhibitions in one visit - Natalia Milosz-Piekarska: Sifted Light alongside Helen Britton: The Story So Far. Lunch on Main Street Mornington after.
editorVerdict: Peninsula-connected jewellery work that reads differently when you know the coast it's drawn from. Worth the detour even if you're not usually a gallery person.
editorNote:
Natalia Milosz-Piekarska makes jewellery and sculpture drawn from her relationship with this coastline - the light, the textures, the specific quality of the Peninsula in every season. Sifted Light is the exhibition of that work.

Run it as a double-bill with Helen Britton: The Story So Far, which is showing simultaneously in the same building. Free entry for both, open Saturday and Sunday 11am to 4pm.

For anyone who lives here or visits regularly, this is the kind of show that reframes what you walk past every day. Mornington Main Street for lunch directly after.
